about: Ark-1 electrical system, the single source of truth for the harness: every component with its real product, position (drone frame: x forward, y left, z up, metres; pos = box centre, yaw about z in degrees) and ports, and every wire from port to port with gauge, colour, connectors and route. Checked by harness.py; drawn by viewer/20_electronics.js. Fields listed in a component's `estimated` are not published by the maker.

power: Pack 12S4P (48 x INR21700-50S, 50.4 V full) -> JBD BMS (low side) -> AS150U arming plug behind the rear hatch
-> Holybro PM08D (I2C V/I sensing, 5.2 V to POWER1) -> 2 mF bulk bank -> Matek FCHUB-12S -> 4 x T-Motor ALPHA 80A (12 AWG, XT60)
FCHUB-12S 5.1 V 5 A BEC -> Pixhawk servo rail (latch servo, NeoPixels, RC-switch logic); FCHUB 12 V 4 A -> pontoon firing driver
Matek BEC12S-PRO @ 12 V -> Jetson Orin Nano DC jack; Matek BEC12S-PRO @ 5.2 V -> Pixhawk POWER2 (backup)
data: ESCs: I/O PWM OUT 1-4 (PWM 400 Hz); ALPHA telemetry lines -> FTDI FT4232H -> Jetson USB
Ethernet Pixhawk <-> Jetson (MAVLink/UDP); TELEM1 RFD900x; TELEM2 RockBLOCK 9603; TELEM3 Ainstein US-D1 radar
GPS1 Holybro M10 (GNSS, compass, safety switch, buzzer); RC IN FrSky R-XSR SBUS; CAN2 -> cargo pogo contacts (DroneCAN)
FMU PWM OUT (AUX): 1 latch servo, 3 firing ARM, 4/5 FIRE L/R, 6/7 pontoon pressure OK L/R (GPIO in, 10 k pull-ups), 8 NeoPixel status + nav chain
LTE Quectel EG25-G (USB) and BMS UART into the Jetson

decisions: Classic stack at the CG: FCHUB-12S on the deck, Pixhawk 6X on 20 mm standoffs and isolators above it; ESC feeds radiate along the arm diagonals.
AS150U anti-spark plug is the arming plug, reached through the rear service hatch that also closes the model's old battery slot.
PM08D carries the full pack current (60 A continuous / 100 A < 60 s) with its XT60s replaced by 8 AWG; it is the 6X's digital power source.
Bulk capacitance 4 x 470 uF / 63 V = 1.88 mF, matching the 2 mF in the SPICE bus model; 63 V parts for a 50.4 V bus.
ALPHA telemetry is not a BLHeli protocol ArduPilot reads, so the four telemetry lines go to the Jetson through an FTDI quad UART.
Jetson Wi-Fi card removed: the RC link uses 2.4 GHz and the Jetson talks through Ethernet/LTE.

Pontoon pin plan from the pontoon system (its Lua hardcodes it): AUX3 ARM interlock, AUX4/AUX5 FIRE L/R into one in-house driver (3 x IRLML6344, ARM in series with each FIRE) on the FCHUB 12 V BEC; each 12 V latch solenoid (0.5 A x 300 ms) releases a Halkey-Roberts head; Multicomp PSF102 pressure switches confirm on AUX6/AUX7.
Cargo pogo contacts carry CAN2 (VCC, CANH, CANL, GND): a smart pod is a DroneCAN node (ID, sensors, release confirm).
LTE and RC antennas sit inside the glass-fibre shell (RF-transparent); RFD900x and Iridium antennas are outside on bulkheads; GNSS on the mast.
Belly loom: radar and cargo cables run down the well beside the pack to IP68 glands in the floor; the inflator leads run down the front legs to glands above the skids.

12S7P (16.1 kg) raises the pack peak to ~108 A: the arming plug is an AMASS AS150U (70 A / 140 A peak) instead of an XT90-S (45 A / 90 A), and the power module is a Holybro PM08D (200 A, 2-14S) instead of a PM02D HV (60 A / 100 A).
